PHASE.NAME: UPGRADE_4 MCP Response Economy
PHASE.GOAL: Implement T2 response summarization with max_tokens and terse mode across high-output MCP handlers.

DATA_FLOWS.FLOW: tools/call arguments carry max_tokens and style to handler-level formatting.
Handlers format full or terse payloads, then a shared response trimmer enforces max_tokens and returns token metadata.
Trimming preserves backward compatibility because max_tokens=0 and style=full keep existing behavior.

STEPS.step-1: Add a shared response trim model with estimated original tokens, shown tokens, was_trimmed, and saved tokens.
STEPS.step-2: Expose max_tokens and style on high-output tool schemas.
STEPS.step-3: Apply terse and max_tokens to semantic_search, graphrag_query, view_signatures, lsp_hover, and lsp_references.
STEPS.step-4: Apply terse and max_tokens to project_status, verify_project, review_code, analyze_logs, mental_test_run, traceability_report, token_savings, and refresh_project.
STEPS.step-5: Apply terse and max_tokens to cascade_impact and cascade_execute outputs.
STEPS.step-6: Add regression tests proving at least 10 MCP tools support max_tokens and style.

VERIFICATION.CHECK: semantic_search max_tokens trims and sets was_trimmed=true.
project_status style=terse returns compact response economy output.
traceability_report style=terse returns response economy metadata and compact text.

RISKS.RISK: Blind text truncation can cut JSON-like content mid-record; trim only final text content while keeping MCP envelope valid.
Different handlers produce different response shapes; normalize summary metadata without forcing one payload schema everywhere.
